what: Alibaba reportedly bans employees from using Claude Code

clean_source_blocks.text: Alibaba has reportedly banned its employees from using Anthropic’s Claude Code at work and instructed them to switch to the Chinese company’s own Qoder coding platform. The decision follows scrutiny of Claude Code features that can inspect user environments and potentially identify people connected to China. It also marks a further escalation in the dispute between Alibaba and Anthropic over the alleged use of Claude to improve competing Chinese AI models. Claude Code is Anthropic’s AI coding assistant for software developers. Despite Anthropic restricting access for users and companies in China, the service has become popular among Chinese programmers. A person familiar with Alibaba’s internal order told Reuters that employees were being directed to replace Claude Code with Qoder, Alibaba’s agentic coding platform. Qoder offers tools for code completion, autonomous development tasks and understanding large software projects.

“As Claude Code was recently discovered to carry back-door risks, after comprehensive evaluation, Claude Code has now been added to a list of high-risk software with security vulnerabilities,” Alibaba said in an internal notice reported by the South China Morning Post. The company recommended employees use Qoder, its own coding agent platform, as a substitute. A Reddit user identified as LegitMichel777 reverse-engineered Claude Code on 30 June and found obfuscated code that had been silently present since version 2.1.91, released on 2 April, with no mention in the release notes. The code checked whether a user’s system timezone was set to Asia/Shanghai or Asia/Urumqi and scanned proxy URLs against a hardcoded list of Chinese domains and AI lab addresses.

Alibaba, the Chinese tech giant, has banned employees from using Anthropic’s AI-powered coding assistant Claude Code in workplace environments, citing alleged security risks involving embedded “backdoors,” according to a person familiar with the matter. The restriction will take effect July 10 and comes amid escalating tensions between the two companies over artificial intelligence security and intellectual property. Alibaba has instructed employees to stop using Claude Code for work and instead adopt Qoder, Alibaba’s in-house AI coding platform, the source said. Alibaba banned Claude Code after security researchers found Anthropic had embedded steganographic tracking code to identify Chinese users. The ban follows Anthropic’s accusation that Alibaba ran the largest known distillation attack on its models. Alibaba has banned its employees from using Claude Code, Anthropic’s AI-powered coding agent, after security researchers discovered that the tool contained hidden code designed to identify Chinese users. The ban, effective 10 July, follows weeks of escalating conflict between the two companies over allegations that Alibaba stole Anthropic’s AI capabilities through industrial-scale distillation.

A person familiar with Alibaba’s internal order told Reuters that employees were being directed to replace Claude Code with Qoder, Alibaba’s agentic coding platform. Qoder offers tools for code completion, autonomous development tasks and understanding large software projects.

Neither Alibaba nor Anthropic immediately commented on the reported ban. Alibaba has also not publicly responded to Anthropic’s earlier accusations against the company.

The ban emerged shortly after developers reported that Claude Code contained mechanisms capable of examining information from a user’s environment.

The tool reportedly checked details including timezone and proxy-related information. Developers also said it could insert subtle markers into prompts before sending them to Anthropic’s servers. These mechanisms could help Anthropic identify users attempting to access Claude from restricted locations or through intermediaries.

An Anthropic employee said on X that the feature was an experiment introduced in March. According to the employee, it was designed to combat account abuse by unauthorized resellers and protect Claude against model-distillation attempts.

The workplace ban comes amid a growing dispute between the two companies.

Anthropic recently accused Alibaba of conducting a large-scale “distillation” effort against Claude. Model distillation involves training a smaller or less capable AI model using answers generated by a more advanced system.

Anthropic claimed Alibaba had illicitly used Claude’s outputs to obtain its capabilities more quickly. It said the effort could accelerate the development of Chinese models toward the performance of its advanced Mythos Preview system. The accusation appeared in a letter sent to two US senators and reviewed by Reuters.

Alibaba has banned its employees from using Claude Code, Anthropic’s AI-powered coding agent, after security researchers discovered that the tool contained hidden code designed to identify Chinese users. The ban, effective 10 July, follows weeks of escalating conflict between the two companies over allegations that Alibaba stole Anthropic’s AI capabilities through industrial-scale distillation.

“As Claude Code was recently discovered to carry back-door risks, after comprehensive evaluation, Claude Code has now been added to a list of high-risk software with security vulnerabilities,” Alibaba said in an internal notice reported by the South China Morning Post. The company recommended employees use Qoder, its own coding agent platform, as a substitute.

A Reddit user identified as LegitMichel777 reverse-engineered Claude Code on 30 June and found obfuscated code that had been silently present since version 2.1.91, released on 2 April, with no mention in the release notes. The code checked whether a user’s system timezone was set to Asia/Shanghai or Asia/Urumqi and scanned proxy URLs against a hardcoded list of Chinese domains and AI lab addresses.

Rather than logging the results conventionally, the system used steganography to hide its signals in the system prompt sent back to Anthropic’s servers. If the timezone was Chinese, the date format changed from dashes to slashes, and the apostrophe in “Today’s date is” was swapped with one of three visually identical but technically distinct Unicode characters depending on which flags were triggered.

payload.title: Alibaba kieltää työntekijöiltään Claude Coden käytön työssä
payload.summary: Alibaba on tiettävästi luokitellut Anthropic-yhtiön Claude Code -ohjelmointiavustajan korkean riskin ohjelmistoksi ja ohjannut työntekijöitään käyttämään sen sijaan omaa Qoder-alustaansa.
payload.content:
Alibaba on tiettävästi kieltänyt työntekijöitään käyttämästä Anthropic-yhtiön Claude Code -ohjelmointiavustajaa työympäristöissä ja ohjannut heitä siirtymään yhtiön omaan Qoder-alustaan. Kielto liittyy huoliin Claude Codeen sisältyneistä ominaisuuksista, joiden on kerrottu voivan tarkastella käyttäjän ympäristöä ja tunnistaa Kiinaan liittyviä käyttäjiä.

## Claude Code lisättiin riskilistalle

Sisäisessä ilmoituksessa Alibaban kerrotaan kuvanneen Claude Codea ohjelmistoksi, jossa on havaittu takaporttiriskejä ja turvallisuushaavoittuvuuksia. Rajoituksen on kerrottu tulevan voimaan 10. heinäkuuta, ja työntekijöitä on lähteiden mukaan kehotettu lopettamaan työkalun käyttö työssä.

Claude Code on Anthropicin ohjelmistokehittäjille suunnattu tekoälyavustaja. Vaikka Anthropic on rajoittanut palvelun saatavuutta Kiinassa oleville käyttäjille ja yrityksille, työkalun kerrotaan saavuttaneen suosiota kiinalaisten ohjelmoijien keskuudessa.

Tapauksen taustalla on myös havaintoja Claude Coden piilotetusta tai peitellystä koodista. Kesäkuun 30. päivänä Reddit-käyttäjä LegitMichel777 kertoi käänteismallintaneensa työkalua ja löytäneensä peiteltyä koodia, jonka kerrottiin olleen mukana versiosta 2.1.91 alkaen. Kyseinen versio oli julkaistu 2. huhtikuuta, eikä muutosta ollut lähteiden mukaan mainittu julkaisutiedoissa.

## Työntekijöitä ohjataan Qoderiin

Löydetyn koodin kerrotaan tarkistaneen, oliko käyttäjän järjestelmän aikavyöhyke asetettu Shanghaihin tai Urumqiin. Lisäksi sen kerrotaan verranneen välityspalvelinten osoitteita kovakoodattuun listaan, jossa oli kiinalaisia verkkotunnuksia ja tekoälylaboratorioiden osoitteita.

Alibaban sisäisen ohjeen mukaan työntekijöiden tulisi korvata Claude Code Qoderilla, joka on yhtiön oma agenttimainen ohjelmointialusta. Qoderin kerrotaan tarjoavan koodintäydennystä, itsenäisten kehitystehtävien tukea ja suurten ohjelmistoprojektien ymmärtämiseen tarkoitettuja työkaluja.

Päätös osuu keskelle Alibaban ja Anthropicin kiristyneitä välejä. Anthropicin on kerrottu syyttäneen Alibabaa sen mallien ominaisuuksien laajamittaisesta kopioinnista eli distillaatiosta kilpailevien kiinalaisten tekoälymallien kehittämiseksi. Alibaba puolestaan perustelee Claude Code -kiellon turvallisuusriskillä.
summary_bullets: Alibaba on tiettävästi kieltänyt Claude Coden käytön työssä ja ohjannut työntekijöitä Qoderiin.
Yhtiö on luokitellut Claude Coden korkean riskin ohjelmistoksi väitettyjen turvallisuushuolien vuoksi.
Päätös liittyy laajempaan kiistaan Alibaban ja Anthropicin välillä tekoälymallien käytöstä ja turvallisuudesta.
